A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoisyRollout work. All 18 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Renamed and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original 7B model training experiments, benchmark comparisons against GRPO, ablations, perception-quality evaluations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds 32B experiments, data-scaling evaluations, rollout-mixture ablations and gradient-contribution measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions mix clean and noisy trajectories for group advantages, condition policy updates on clean inputs, and anneal Gaussian noise. The objectives and Algorithm 1 remain equivalent. Newly specified token-mean loss aggregation and expanded reward-format wording document implementation details without establishing a changed proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Training still uses Geometry3K and K12, renamed MMK12. Evaluation retains Geometry3K, MathVerse, MathVision, MathVista, WeMath and HallusionBench. Larger subsets and model sizes change experimental settings, not task or domain coverage. Medical, robotic and assistive applications are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add LLaVA-OneVision-7B, Kimi-VL-16B, MM-Eureka-Zero-38B and MM-Eureka-Qwen-32B. Table 6 adds the GRPO comparator with upper clipping 0.28. Existing large-model comparators are relocated, and v1's Dr. GRPO result rows reappear as GRPO without std(r). The untuned Qwen7B comparator is removed from the K12 noise study, although retained elsewhere.

E3.justification: The main K12/MMK12 setting changes from 2.1K samples and 60 steps to 6.4K and 120 steps for 7B. v2 adds 32B configurations, a 1.1K–6.4K data sweep, and mixture-ratio, clipping and masked-gradient protocols. Seed and MMK12 noise tables switch from six-benchmark averages to five-benchmark OOD averages. Table 1 also revises VLAA-Thinker's stated training budget from 126K SFT plus 25K RL to 25K RL, without establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds data-size sensitivity analysis (Figure 6), clean/noisy mixture proportions (Table 11), higher-clipping compatibility (Table 6), and gradient-contribution analysis (Section 3.4 and Appendix J). Figure 9 adds quantitative training curves for cropping and rotation failures already described in v1. Existing temperature, annealing and noise-strength studies and both case studies remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Table 9 reports data seed 3 alongside the previously reported seeds 1, 2 and 42. Appendix J specifies averaging five independent update runs for the new gradient analysis. Figure 8 includes shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning. This expands statistical reporting without introducing comprehensive benchmark confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original 7B/Geometry3K headline scores are retained, while v2 adds 32B, larger-MMK12, scaling, mixture, clipping and gradient results under new settings. Existing values also change: the default six-benchmark average is corrected from 58.6 to 58.5 (v1 Table 2/v2 Table 3), the 16-rollout OOD average changes from 58.6 to 58.9 (v1 Table 4/v2 Table 8), and seed-1 GRPO MathVerse changes from 50.1 to 50.8 (v1 Table 7/v2 Table 9). Geometry3K results are removed from the K12 noise table.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendix J introduce mathematical definitions of anchor updates, subgroup-specific parameter changes and their projection ratios. Existing GRPO objectives and annealing mathematics remain equivalent up to notation and parameterization. No convergence theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction now explicitly claim effectiveness across 7B/32B models and approximately 1K–6K training scales. This extends the stated generalizability claim while retaining the central contributions: mixed visual rollouts, noise annealing, sample efficiency, strong benchmark performance and no additional training overhead.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of noisy-gradient contributions and balanced rollout mixtures, attributes smaller 32B gains to prior RL tuning, and expands the explanation of unsuccessful input-conditioned updates. Appendix G explicitly limits evidence to modest model/data scales and acknowledges missing exploration and convergence guarantees. Appendix F adds prospective applications. The gradient discussion overstates consistency: Figure 8 ends with the clean contribution higher.

D1.justification: Appendix K newly specifies AdamW, token-mean loss aggregation, CPU memory, per-step training times and detailed configurations for each model/dataset combination. Appendix J documents selected model modules, five-step masked updates and matched training batches. These substantially expand reproducibility information; existing prompts and code/model/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Kimi-VL, MEGA-Bench, Skywork R1V/R1V2, VisualPRM and off-policy guidance, and more explicitly positions visual augmentation as complementary to optimization-focused RL changes. The established VLM/RL research lineage remains, with most detailed related work moved to Appendix E. Citation renumbering alone is presentational.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with explicit mechanism and contribution lists. Experimental setup is reorganized, and the algorithm, templates, unsuccessful attempts and detailed related work move into dedicated appendices. The original A.1–A.4 appendix structure becomes A–K, alongside extensive terminology and prose editing.

P2.justification: The main comparison table is split into moderate- and large-model tables, its average column is removed, and rollout-budget results become a separate expanded table. New scaling, gradient and augmentation plots and mixture/configuration tables substantially extend the displays. Existing figures, algorithm and prompt boxes are relocated or resized; the original case-study content is retained.

improvement.justification: v1's validation was confined to 7B models and 2.1K training subsets. v2's 32B comparisons, data-size sweeps and mixture ablations substantially strengthen evidence for generalizability and the central design choices. Appendices J–K improve reproducibility, while Appendix G states important limits. These gains outweigh localized reporting defects: Table 11's 9/12 row averages about 58.2 rather than the stated 57.9, and Figure 8 contradicts the claim that noisy contributions are consistently larger.
